query: How does AMD define its Data Center reporting segment and what products are included
normalized: amd center data define included products reporting segment

output.content:
AMD defines its **Data Center** reporting segment as the business that primarily supplies compute, acceleration and networking products for data-center deployments. The segment is designed to address computational processing, visual-data processing and AI-workload acceleration requirements in data centers. [[1]] 

The products included are: 
- **Server CPUs**, principally **AMD EPYC** processors. [[1]]
- **Data-center GPUs and AI accelerators**, principally **AMD Instinct** products, including MI200, MI300, MI325 and MI350-series accelerators; AMD also identifies Radeon PRO V Series as a data-center graphics brand. [[1]]
- **APUs** and other **data-center SoC products**. [[1]]
- **DPUs**, including AMD Pensando DPUs, which offload infrastructure services from host CPUs. [[1]]
- **AI NICs**, including Pensando Pollara 400 and Vulcano products for GPU-cluster connectivity. [[1]]
- **FPGAs and adaptive SoCs**, such as Virtex, Kintex, Artix, Spartan, Zynq and Versal devices, along with Alveo acceleration cards. [[1]] 

AMD’s filing therefore treats the segment as broader than just server processors or AI GPUs: it encompasses the compute, programmable-logic, acceleration and networking building blocks used in enterprise, cloud, hyperscale and other data-center systems. [[1]]

sources.title: February 4, 2026 - 10-K: Annual report [Section 13 and 15(d), not S-K Item 405]
